description: This figure group is a single table rendered as an image — no micrographs, plots or spectra are present. It reports point-wise elemental composition of a spark-plasma-sintered (SPSed) non-equiatomic high-entropy steel. The header has two rows: 'Sample condition' and 'Scan area' on the left, then a merged heading 'Elemental composition (wt.%)' spanning five element columns labelled Fe, Mn, Ni, Al and Si. Only one sample condition is listed, 'SPSed sample', analysed at two locations, Spot 1 and Spot 2. Spot 1 gives Fe 32.46, Mn 10.00, Ni 32.09, Al 21.82 and Si 2.63 wt.%; Spot 2 gives Fe 44.53, Mn 21.60, Ni 20.66, Al 7.33 and Si 5.88 wt.%. The two spots differ strongly: Ni and Al are enriched at Spot 1, whereas Fe and Mn are enriched at Spot 2, indicating that the sintered microstructure is chemically heterogeneous on the micrometre scale rather than a single homogeneous solid solution. Carbon, although part of the nominal alloy, is not tabulated, and no uncertainties, detection limits or number of measurements are given. No axis, legend or scale bar exists because the panel is purely tabular.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel (WDS point analysis) with columns 'Sample condition', 'Scan area' and 'Elemental composition (wt.%)' subdivided into Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si; two data rows for 'SPSed sample' at Spot 1 and Spot 2.

observations.observation: The figure is a two-row data table, not a plot: columns are sample condition, scan area and elemental composition (wt.%) for Fe, Mn, Ni, Al and Si.
Only one sample condition is tabulated, 'SPSed sample', measured at two scan areas, 'Spot 1' and 'Spot 2'.
Spot 1 composition: Fe 32.46 wt.%, Mn 10.00 wt.%, Ni 32.09 wt.%, Al 21.82 wt.%, Si 2.63 wt.%.
Spot 2 composition: Fe 44.53 wt.%, Mn 21.60 wt.%, Ni 20.66 wt.%, Al 7.33 wt.%, Si 5.88 wt.%.
Ni (32.09 vs 20.66 wt.%) and Al (21.82 vs 7.33 wt.%) are higher at Spot 1, while Fe (44.53 vs 32.46 wt.%), Mn (21.60 vs 10.00 wt.%) and Si (5.88 vs 2.63 wt.%) are higher at Spot 2.
No carbon column is present in the table, although the alloy designation in the paper's title and abstract includes C1.
The table carries no stated measurement uncertainty, detection limit, accelerating voltage, or number of analysed points.
The caption states the composition was obtained by point WDS analysis of the SPSed sample of the non-equiatomic HES.

The paper's abstract states the nominal alloy is Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 processed by mechanical alloying (35 h) and spark plasma sintering; the table's wt.% values are not directly comparable to that at.% nominal composition without conversion.
